decisions.reason: Removing the monthly approved-clip quota makes the gate's quota-counting rule obsolete, while its review and publication rules remain independently meaningful.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
I had to end the contract. With tomorrow being the 1-month mark and only 1 clip delivered, despite me reaching out 3 times, I wasn't left with another option. This isn't personal — I just have to hold the same standard for everyone on the team, and the milestones exist for a reason.

I'm sorry it ended this way. If circumstances were different on your end, I get that life happens — but I need clippers I can count on to communicate, even if it's just to say "I'm behind" or "I need more time."

Wishing you well with whatever's next. If you ever want to try again down the line and things look different for you, the door's not permanently closed.

decisions.reason: Ending the contract and removing the monthly quota does not change the independently defined standard that a clip deliver a complete standalone lesson.
The source does not resolve or change the clip-duration limits or their existing ambiguity.
The contract termination does not change which source videos are permitted when clips are produced.
The source does not replace or cancel any submission channel, folder, access, or review-link rule.
Ending the later contract does not retroactively alter the qualification method or success criteria.
The source reinforces the communication expectation and its failure; it does not change the expectation's value, and the same-message evidence is already represented.
The source does not modify the clean-editing, effects, or transition standards.
The source does not change any caption color, font, effects, lettering, or positioning rule.
The contract termination does not alter the standard for selecting strong and impactful moments.
The source contains no decision about wind-noise removal or audio cleanup.
